stops.note: 'island'; also a Roman apartment block standing in its street grid like an island
the medical student Paul Langerhans described clusters of cells in the pancreas in his Berlin dissertation of 1869, later named 'islets' after him
the Belgian physiologist Jean de Meyer named the islets' supposed hormone in 1909, before anyone had isolated it
Frederick Banting and Charles Best isolated it in Toronto in 1921, and 14-year-old Leonard Thompson became the first person treated, in January 1922

current_meaning: a hormone that regulates blood sugar, used to treat diabetes
